quest.title: Through the Predawn Night
quest.description: As agreed, you and the others gather in the village chief's house to hold a meeting...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x775, Mora x31175, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

chapter.title: Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Stay safe, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I'll be here praying for you. Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Has everyone arrived?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Everyone is already waiting inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, what're we waiting for! Let's join them!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Please wait a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Before attending the meeting, I hope you can promise me one thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Promise me that you won't commit to anything too reckless.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... what do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll try not to.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone's here so early! But why isn't anybody talking?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We already discussed things a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey, where've you been? I've missed you two!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can start now.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Very well.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After some discussion and debates, the group finally works out a detailed plan together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure this is gonna work?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I gotta admit, it's bold. Color me impressed!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hm... It's worth a try.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The point of discussion is to arrive at a solution. Let's cut the small talk and move to the next point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you're making Paimon nervous...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: You're finally done.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I have some other stuff to take care of. Catch you all later!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: C'mon, don't gimme that face! I know what you're going to say. I'll be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: That's what I wanted to hear. Take care.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, Paimon... Judging from your expressions, the meeting must've been quite productive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can tell?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I'm not good at scheming or strategy, but I can sense people's emotions. And based on your reaction, things must have gone quite well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll make our move on the next Jnagarbha Day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's a little worried... Hopefully, nothing will go wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: To be honest, I feel the same... But you're already some of the most capable people I know. So, you have my trust.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hoho... Candace gave us a compliment!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Your deeds speak for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace, we stayed behind to tell you that although you won't be coming with us, we'll be sure to remember your words.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I'm very glad to hear that.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I've said the same thing to everyone here today as I said to you when you arrived: Your safety is the most important thing.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Only when you're safe can the plan be successful. So please, take care.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Candace.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: You're welcome. And thank you for taking my advice.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Good luck... with everything. I'll be here in the village praying for you.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, sounds good. I'll go make some preparations.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alhaitham!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Have you finished saying your goodbyes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, also Candace told everyone to be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes, she did. But I think my point also bears repeating.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Our plan is not child's play. We won't be able to achieve anything if we're simply careful. We must go beyond that and fully commit ourselves to it.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I hope this is clear to you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I understand and accept.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Shouldn't you be saying something more cheerful to boost our morale right now?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Didn't we already do that during the meeting?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can never have enough words of encouragement!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In that case, Candace can coddle you to your heart's content, while I continue to remind you of the seriousness of our situation.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We all have our jobs to do, after all. It's like how some people can be put in charge of logistics, while others will fight on the front lines.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, speaking of the front lines... you don't look anything like a soldier.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Of course. Compared to the mercenaries, I'm merely a feeble scholar.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: But the advantage of not being a mercenary is that I get to stay in a safer place and offer my strategic insight.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Just think about that mercenary who lost his mind. Mercenary groups are facing constant danger every single day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, being a scholar is also a high-risk occupation... And you are a scholar!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I'm not like the rest of them. Even among members of the same species, some will exhibit far more potential than others.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This guy... Hmph, Paimon still remembers when those mercenaries in Port Ormos called you a lunatic!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: All intellectuals are lunatics in the eyes of fools. I'll take that as a compliment.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: That reminds me...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you remember the record we saw in the King Deshret Ruins? It mentioned forbidden knowledge.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You have a good memory.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Forbidden knowledge has the power to drive people insane, but this fact has never been shared with the public. Even I, who has worked in the Akademiya for some time, was never once informed of this.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I think... those mad scholars and mercenaries we encountered may have all fallen victim to the corrupting qualities of forbidden knowledge.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: But the Akademiya has always held a different view. They have always believed that symptoms of madness are a side effect of human contact with divine knowledge as mere mortals.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Come to think of it, perhaps the Akademiya has also never understood the true nature of forbidden knowledge, and thus always approached the issue from the wrong direction...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: The Withering, Eleazar, and the sandstorms... Don't you think what is happening right now across Sumeru is rather similar to the forbidden knowledge pollution that occurred in the desert thousands of years ago?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Paimon thought that Irminsul's disease is what caused the Withering and the sandstorms.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: At least, that was what Tighnari told us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a second! Could it be that...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Ah, you've connected the dots. The cause of Irminsul's illness may precisely be the pollution from forbidden knowledge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...B—But if that's the case, what should we do? This is huge...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We must tell Nahida about this as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Wait, why do you think Lesser Lord Kusanali would have a solution to this situation?

choices.text: She said the key to saving Irminsul is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean, it's related to the scene you saw when you passed out in the Avidya Forest? That whole "...the world... forget me..." thing?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: In that case, it's imperative that we rescue Lesser Lord Kusanali. Only by working with her to save Irminsul can we completely resolve the problems Sumeru currently faces.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's right.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: To make sure we're still on track, I would like to check on the state of some of our preparatory work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where are we going?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: To an Eremite base.

choices.text: Contained within the remaining consciousness of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.
Another occurrence of forbidden knowledge pollution...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Wait... seriously? Remember...? We went into the desert not long ago to exchange hostages with the Eremites. Once we arrived, the ground collapsed due to an earthquake, and we fell into some ruins? Still nothing?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Come on...! It was a remnant of King Deshret's bygone civilization and we found some messages left by a priest of the King, and learned about the existence of forbidden knowledge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! It's all coming back now. Thanks for reminding us.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Ah, they're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, what are they doing here!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I gave them some technical work to do.

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: Oh? It's the Scribe... and is that the Traveler I see?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: How's the work going?

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: Ah, yes! We have fixed the devices according to your instructions! One of them is already ready for use, while the others are still under repair.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aren't those devices for Canned Knowledge extraction? What are you doing with those?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, look here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh! M—More Canned Knowledge!? Are you going to put more weird stuff into {NICKNAME}'s head again?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What's that look on your face? Are you scared?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's a little scared, but very very furious!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hmm. That's an interesting response.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Anyway, we're not going to use this just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As I mentioned during the meeting, this knowledge capsule contains a decree I drew up in the past. The Akademiya should also have their own copy. And according to the plan we just came up with...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... I want you to record something into this capsule.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Me?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Do you believe we can save Lesser Lord Kusanali?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Good. Conviction is the most important part of all of this.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Now, please get ready, and put on this device.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You want us to record our conviction into the knowledge capsule?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Paimon is still really worried...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I understand, but trust me, Paimon, this is something we have to do. It's best if you can do as I say.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Because to achieve this impossible task, it sounds like you'll need to fool your own heart first. Although it may feel like a trick, self-encouragement may be the most important tool we have.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon can see the point you're trying to make...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm ready.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Please imagine this: We have orchestrated our plan and successfully rescued Lesser Lord Kusanali. As a result, we have changed Sumeru's entire political landscape.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Everything went without a hitch, and everyone recognizes and praises our achievements.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure... Okay...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Now, open your eyes.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's this...?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Read it out loud.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Some stirring words have been written on the note.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Although you don't quite understand the purpose of this recording, you still follow Alhaitham's instructions for the sake of the plan.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It's done.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What a fascinating experience...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is your head okay? Does anything hurt?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm fine.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It's just a recording. There should be no negative effects.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, what was the point of doing this? Paimon doesn't get it...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: And that's perfectly fine. In any case, these capsules aren't meant to be used by you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Have you forgotten? Our plan needs to account for those who have long relied on the Akasha.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You may find it hard to believe, but for those people, everything the Akasha transmits to them is nothing short of absolute truth.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Imagine if you've been using a device like the Akasha since the day you were born. And this device has always supported you during times of need...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: After all that time, what do you think you'd become?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... A fool? A machine?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: A slave to orders.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: And that's why rules are so important.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: In addition, those who understand the rules can delineate boundaries, and identify gray areas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... but why would you need to identify the gray areas?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You could say that those kinds of ambiguous zones can be very interesting. One might even say they're advantageous in the right hands...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The things you're interested in are all really out there... Are all Sumeru scholars like this?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Anyway, that's enough chitchat.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I'm going to take those two to work on some small projects. You can head to Caravan Ribat and start preparing for the next step.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Small projects?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: We are going to tinker with the Akasha Terminal and make a few modifications.

choices.text: What I may lack in faith, I'll make up with my actions.

talks.objective: Go to Caravan Ribat and meet up with Cyno

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I thought we agreed on a plan. How can you go back on your word?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The plan is too radical and carries a high risk for casualties. I've given it a lot of thought, and in the end, I still can't agree to it.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: But it's still the best plan we have. As a former matra, you of all people should be able to see the bigger picture, and recognize the innate advantages of our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I did, and that's how I saw the danger behind these so-called advantages. Alhaitham's plan is even more radical than I imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you guys arguing?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: My friend, you're just in time. Why don't you help me persuade Cyno... He's turned against our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We agreed to work out a plan at the meeting. As mercenaries, you're familiar with the local environment, so you'll take care of the specifics. But then, you went to Alhaitham for suggestions...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Had I known Alhaitham would give you those kinds of suggestions, I would not have agreed to the plan.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Look, you already know that we're all on the same side here, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Mercenaries place a lot of importance on their bonds of friendship, but also will not hesitate to make sacrifices if they deem the situation to be sufficiently dire. I'm sorry, but as things stand, I can't accept your principles.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Seems you really do understand the ways of the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, this is also something you should know.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Rahman's plan is to have me work with the Caravan Ribat guards in my capacity as a matra. We'll arrest the mercenaries and escort them into Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, how can we work with the guards!?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: We can't get through that wall easily, remember? Caravan Ribat would never let so many unregistered members of the Eremites enter Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: My plan will clear us of any possible suspicion, and also let us enter the city as a big group. There is no better way.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That also sounds like something Alhaitham told you. Am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Doesn't Alhaitham know how dangerous this plan is!?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Of course he does... He told me, "There is no perfect plan, but this can get the job done."

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: #He also said that with the help of Cyno and {NICKNAME}, our chance of success would increase significantly.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I never blindly trust anyone, and I've always had a good eye for people. I think he made a number of valid points. It's my own choice to trust you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If I make the arrests alone, I can control myself and prevent you from getting hurt, but I can't guarantee that kind of discipline from the guards.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: To make the whole thing more convincing, you'll need to resist to some degree. Casualties are inevitable once push comes to shove.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm okay with the deaths of enemies, but now that we're allies, I'm against the meaningless loss of our own.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: ...Haha.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I can't believe a matra would actually care about us. I've lived a hard life, and I can say that people like you are hard to come by.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I've always treated my allies with honesty and respect. They have the right to know important things like this.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: ...Now, you're making this hard for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, is there something we can do to help?

choices.text: If there is no other way...

response.speaker: Rahman
response.text: Haha, I knew you would say that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We can help "fight" some of the mercenaries, which should reduce the number of times you'll have to struggle directly with the guards. That should help at least a little bit!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We should respect the determination of Rahman and his comrades.

response.speaker: Rahman
response.text: Cyno, on behalf of my people, I thank you for your kindness. But this is a mission we cannot turn our backs on. We strongly value the lives of our friends, but the goal we are about to achieve is even more important.

response.speaker: Rahman
response.text: We have no fear of casualties, because we crave the spoils of victory. So, please lend us your support! We will show you the determination of us desert-dwellers.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...Well, now that you've put it that way, I can no longer refuse.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: But remember, you need to follow the plan and not do anything reckless. Candace made it very clear that we can only achieve our goals if we can ensure our safety.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Since you and I both recognize the significance of this operation, there should be no more animosity between the followers of the Dendro Archon and those of King Deshret. Everyone's life is equally important.

response.speaker: Rahman
response.text: Okay, you have a deal. Let's do this for our shared dream!

choices.text: I can help. I know what I'm doing.

talks.objective: Talk to the soldiers stationed in Caravan Ribat

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Guards.

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: General Mahamatra!? T—To what do we owe the honor?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Keep your voice down.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This is a secret operation. I'm going to arrest a large criminal gang near this location. According to the Akademiya's Guide and Regulations on Secret Operations, I have the right to ask for the cooperation of Caravan Ribat.

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: Ah, of course, of course! Mahamatra Cyno's order is the Akademiya's order. Just let us know what you need.

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: But who exactly are you planning to arrest, and how many people are you expecting? Depending on the scale of this operation, we may need to report it to our superiors.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: They're a squad of Eremites whose number is comparable to Ayn Al-Ahmar in Port Ormos. They're involved in the theft and resale of supplies from the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: As many as Ayn Al-Ahmar!? This should definitely be classified as a joint operation.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Then I suggest that you report this to your superiors as soon as possible, and treat it as a top-priority desert operation. I will need personnel.

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: Got it! Please wait a moment. I will contact them immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You look so commanding when you're working.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Because this is work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're much more friendly to us.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Because I trust you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe you're still in the mood to chat. This whole thing has Paimon scared stiff!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aren't you even a little worried? What if these guards already know that you have betrayed the Akademiya, and are no longer their General Mahamatra...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even if that guard doesn't know, their superiors might, right?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We discussed this, remember?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Caravan Ribat operation is of great importance. But don't worry, the guards there shouldn't know that Cyno has stepped down.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: How can you be so sure?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: First, the other matra still don't know why Cyno has left, which proves that the Akademiya has been covering up the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Second, this is a crucial moment for the Akademiya's god creation plan. If something were to happen to the General Mahamatra, it's bound to attract a lot of unwanted attention.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: No matter how you look at it, they don't seem interested in sharing the news of Cyno's departure.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...A reasonable inference. I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Which brings us to our next issue: I'm sure some of you have been wondering if the prediction function of the Akasha will affect our operation.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Akasha is still in operation, so I must remain on high alert.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Actually, considering the power of the Akasha, it's quite strange that it hasn't already tried to interfere with my actions.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I've given that a lot of thought. For now, I don't think you'll need to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If you remember, when you first came to Aaru Village, all your actions and routes were predicted by the Akasha. It even gave that information to those who kidnapped the Village Keepers.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: #But things like that never happened again after we met up with {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hm...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's true. But why?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Look at it from a different angle. Why do you think the Akasha will predict your actions?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Because my personal data has been entered into the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's true, but, the key to this question is, how well can the Akasha make predictions about a person?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Haven't you ever thought about it? Just how can it do this in the first place?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Because the Akasha controls the entirety of Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Akademiya firmly believes that all human actions can be explained through logic.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: By sorting and analyzing entered data, the Akasha can derive behavioral logic, and predict the actions of those who fit an existing logic model.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: However, at the risk of sounding like an advocate for fallacies, can everyone truly be considered "logical" at all times?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Emotions are a part of our behavioral logic. But can you guarantee that every experience of the same joy or pain would be equally intense? How can our feelings and opinions be predictable down to the letter in every single instance?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Cyno, in the past, you've always worked alone. In the absence of another person who could sway you or your thoughts, the Akasha could produce predictions that were similar to your real-life behavioral principles.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Decisive and principled, you were used to solving problems alone. That's why the Akasha could figure you out.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But now, you've joined a team. And I believe the Akasha hasn't yet figured out the full composition of it.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Our thoughts and logic have intermingled, and weaved themselves together to become a complicated, chaotic mess. Any one of us could potentially disagree with another.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Akasha lacks data on these interactions, and it's impossible for it to predict your actions in the future based on your decisions in the past. After all, there's probably a limit to just how much we can be modeled or controlled by data.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So, in my opinion, you're probably safe for now.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Makes sense to me, I agree. The Akasha is not alive, and I don't think we can be completely controlled by something without a mind of its own.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Hm, is that so.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I guess there are things that even the Akasha cannot calculate, and people will not be forever trapped by the past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... Paimon's so glad that this is settled!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Next time, pay attention during our meetings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waah, will do...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm confident that we can do this.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Just remember to stay vigilant.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, footsteps!
General Mahamatra! We were not expecting your presence here.

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: I'm the Security Officer of the Great Red Sand District. My name is Luxembarbo.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: #Mm. This is my assistant, {NICKNAME}. {F#She}{M#He} will be working with me. The construct next to {F#her}{M#him} is for {F#her}{M#his} work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Beep! Construct! Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: #What a great honor to meet you, {NICKNAME}! Your golden hair is as bright as the sun! And... uh, is this the latest technology from the Akademiya...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Have you made a decision regarding the matter I mentioned to your subordinate?

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: It seems to be a dire situation, so of course, you will have our full cooperation. To be perfectly honest, I've always longed to go on a mission with someone as well-known as yourself...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's no need for flattery.

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Y—Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Take your most elite platoon and follow me to the eastern side of the district. We will carry out the operation there.

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Understood!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: *sigh* Map?

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Hurry, bring the map!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A guard immediately brings over a map. Cyno circles the location of the operation on it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: In two days, we will engage Rahman's Eremites, and capture all of them.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Any questions about the time or location?

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: None at all, sir.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Good. See you then.

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe hanging around the General Mahamatra isn't so bad after all! Everyone's so respectful towards us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, it does feel pretty good.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This is all due to the absolute authority of the Akademiya. And now, we're going to strike back against that massive pillar of power.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Get ready. We will move out in two days.

talks.objective: Wait until the appointed time (two days later)

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: They're all waiting for you.

talks.objective: Go to the east side of the desert

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! Over there! Our helpers have arrived already!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's hurry over!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Wait a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaah! It's you!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're my assistant, remember?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, I remember.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Being my assistant, you must stay with me. Now, let's head over there.

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: It's General Mahamatra and his assistants!

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: We meet again!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're here early.

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: It's to show how important we think this operation is.

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Since this is a big case for the Akademiya, we are prepared to give it our best.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm glad to hear your sense of resolve. Remember, we must capture them alive.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: They are our only leads for the case. If they die, we will be unable to continue the investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Understood!

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: Everyone! The Eremites are approaching from the west!

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Make preparations and be ready for combat!

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Halt!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Oh? What a warm welcome. What do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Judging from those shiny weapons in your hands, it seems like you're not interested in a deal?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Rahman, the Akademiya has caught wind of your smuggling and illicit sales. If you value your life, I advise you to surrender.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Who're you supposed to be? A matra from the Akademiya? Hah, I can't believe you came all this way just to catch us...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm not here to talk.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Nobody's given me this much time of day since I became a mercenary.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Brothers! For that slight, let's wash our blades with their blood! Let's show them we Eremites are not to be messed with!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's over!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Aghhh!

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: We have subdued them! The operation is now over, all Eremite mercenaries and related personnel in the area have been arrested!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Argh! You pitiful Dendro Archon dogs... You'll regret this!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmph, I'm afraid you'll regret it first.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: King Deshret will curse you, and you will all...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Silence!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Oh! Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Restrain them and take them back to Caravan Ribat! Count their numbers and send them to the Akademiya as instructed by the General Mahamatra!

dialogues.speaker: Gaete
dialogues.text: Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The guards escort a furious-looking Rahman and the others away...

dialogues.speaker: Luxembarbo
dialogues.text: Mahamatra Cyno, I will now take my leave. If you need further assistance, please come to Caravan Ribat and ask for me.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Understood. You are dismissed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There they go...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Let's talk elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You find a safe place free of potential eavesdroppers and begin your conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This part of the plan went really well!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. Things went perfectly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's fantastic!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that punch you gave Rahman there sure looked convincing enough...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Once we're done here, I'll return to Caravan Ribat and oversee the group's transport. I promise I'll get everyone into Sumeru City safely.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're the reason why everything went so well!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's not the time to celebrate yet. Hmm, I believe Dehya should already be waiting for you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Go join up with her. She will need you to introduce her to Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, is it really okay for us not to share the full plan with Tighnari? What if he'll feel miffed about it, and refuse to work with us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm a little worried about that, too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I have a very close relationship with Tighnari. Given how well we know each other, I believe my message alone should be enough to bring him to our side. He knows I won't make jokes about things like this.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If we need help, Tighnari is the best option.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Get ready for the next phase of the plan. Don't keep them waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's time for the operation. Let's go meet Cyno in the desert!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The guards should be stationed in the courtyard nearby. You can find them there.
